lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: multiplicative comparison

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: Use the standard algorithm to calculate 247 × 36.

steps: Multiply 247 by 30 to get 7410; the tens-place zero keeps the place value.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: Estimate 876 × 94 by rounding 876 to the nearest hundred and 94 to the nearest ten.
Subtract 6 from 71. Then multiply the difference by 12. Which numerical expression represents the calculation?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Without evaluating it, which statement describes (47 - 11) × 7?
choices: Multiply the difference between 11 and 47 by 7.
Multiply the difference between 47 and 11 by 7.
Subtract 11 from the product of 47 and 7.
Subtract the product of 11 and 7 from 47.

items.prompt: An event has 14 display tables. Each table holds 8 boxes with 72 items in each box. There are also 3 loose items. How many items are in inventory altogether?
Maya has 7 times as many cards as Leo. Leo has 74 cards. How many cards does Maya have?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: An area model for 5775 × 28 splits 5775 into 5000 + 700 + 70 + 5 and 28 into 20 + 8. What total product does the model represent?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Use partial products to calculate 9610 × 91. Decompose both factors by place value, multiply each pair of parts, and add the partial products. What is the product?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
